# Cybersecurity Industry Hiring Analysis — Executive Summary
**Week of March 22, 2026**

---

This week's analysis tracked 249 cybersecurity and adjacent technology companies, successfully retrieving job listing data from 26 of them. The remaining 223 companies returned no usable data due to a known scraper limitation: the majority of enterprise career pages rely on JavaScript-rendered frameworks that our automated tooling cannot currently process. This means the absence of job data for those companies reflects a technical constraint, not a signal of hiring inactivity. All strategic insights in this summary are drawn exclusively from the 26 companies where data was successfully collected, representing a meaningful but partial snapshot of the broader market.

Among the companies where data was retrieved, the dominant theme this week is the industry-wide acceleration toward **agentic AI and AI-native product architectures**. This is no longer a peripheral feature conversation — it is a core platform strategy across virtually every major vendor in the dataset. CrowdStrike is staffing a distinct AI-native Detection and Response (AIDR) product line, including native identity and authentication capabilities built directly into the platform. Okta is treating Agentic AI and Non-Human Identity (NHI) as dedicated, standalone product areas, signaling that machine and agent identity management is rapidly becoming a first-class security domain. Elastic Security is investing in an "Elastic Agent Builder" platform to support enterprise LLM-powered workflows, while Datadog — the largest single employer in the dataset at 457 open positions — is building proprietary foundation models trained on observability telemetry and autonomous AI agents designed for SRE incident response, with a roadmap extending into security response and self-healing infrastructure. Frontegg, though small in headcount, is making an architecturally bold bet on MCP (Model Context Protocol) as a standard for AI agent-to-API communication, positioning itself as infrastructure-layer plumbing for the agentic AI ecosystem. Taken together, these signals suggest the industry is past the experimentation phase — vendors are now committing engineering headcount and product roadmaps to AI-native architectures at scale.

The second major theme is **geographic and platform expansion among growth-stage vendors**. Wiz (191 open positions, health score 8/10) is expanding from cloud posture management into active application security testing via an AI-driven DAST capability, while simultaneously investing in AI security research as a dedicated product domain — a notable broadening of scope for a company that built its brand on agentless cloud scanning. Axonius (health score 8/10) is similarly shifting from single-product asset management toward a multi-product platform strategy with deeper threat and vulnerability intelligence. Arctic Wolf is executing a deliberate geographic push into U.S. Midwest and Northeast enterprise markets, as well as the DACH region in Europe. Cato Networks, following its acquisition of Aim Security, is building a distinct AI Security product line within its SASE platform, targeting enterprise risks like prompt injection, AI tool data leakage, and AI supply chain exposure. On the cautionary side, companies like Sonrai Security, Indigo, and Archer (via Broadcom) show minimal hiring activity, though it is important to note this may reflect scraper limitations as much as organic business conditions. Overall, the data suggests a market bifurcating between well-capitalized platforms accelerating aggressively into AI-native capabilities and smaller or more specialized vendors operating in a consolidation or steady-state mode.
